sections.html:
Franklin is the Williamson County seat, about 21 miles south of Nashville along the Harpeth River. About 90,226 people lived here in July 2025, up 8.0 percent from the 83,454 counted in 2020. The city has been growing for decades, and the north side has filled with houses and offices.

Prices run high. The typical owner-occupied house is valued at $705,400 for the 2020 to 2024 period, more than double the $332,700 national median. Of the city's 33,998 households, 63.8 percent own their home. Owners with a mortgage report monthly costs of $2,542, owners without one report $712, and renters pay a median of $1,923. Median household income is $119,528.

Buyers here tend to be long-term owners with large price tags in mind, so a clean title and tidy paperwork matter. Interstate 65 crosses the eastern side of the city, and Mack Hatcher Parkway circles the business district. If your house sits near the square or inside one of the five historic districts on the National Register, call City Hall before planning exterior repairs, because local ordinance protects older buildings and neighborhoods.

The city charges $0.296 for each $100 of assessed value, and the 2026-27 budget proposal leaves that unchanged. The rate has two parts: a $0.2310 base for operations and debt, plus $0.0650 added after the last reappraisal for infrastructure and city services. The city calls it one of the lowest rates in Tennessee. The county assessor reappraises every four years.

One bill covers three taxing bodies. The Williamson County Trustee collects for the county, the Franklin Special School District and the city together, so a Franklin owner does not get a separate city statement. Ask the trustee at 615-790-5709 for the full figure on a specific parcel, and call the assessor at 615-790-5708 about assessed value or the mailing address on a bill.

The trustee cannot waive, prorate or release any tax or interest. Whoever owned the property on January 1 is the owner of record who gets the bill, so a seller closing mid-year has to pass the bill along to the buyer through the closing statement.

Payment runs on a fixed calendar each year. Pay before March and you owe no interest.

Williamson County tax bill calendar
DateWhat happens
Early OctoberStatements are mailed
First Monday of OctoberPayment opens
End of FebruaryLast day to pay without interest
March 11.5 percent interest starts and repeats on the first of every later month

If you list a house in the fall, a buyer's title company will want to see whether the current bill is paid or still open. Keep your statement handy and tell the closing agent early if you have not received one.

sections.h2: Schools, utilities and city fees buyers ask about
sections.html:
Most of the city belongs to the Franklin Special School District for kindergarten through eighth grade, and high school students attend Williamson County Schools. Outlying parts of the city are in the county district for every grade. Families often start a house search with the school boundary, so be ready to say which district serves your address. Private options include Battle Ground Academy, Franklin Classical School, Franklin Christian Academy, Montessori School of Franklin, New Hope Academy and Thales Academy.

Monthly costs come up next. Residential trash and recycling is set to rise by $1 to $34 a month in fiscal 2027, and stormwater fees are projected to add about $20.70 a year for most homes. Water and sewer rates rose 6 percent and 5.7 percent on January 1, 2026.

The city's water department serves most residents, though pockets are served by the Mallory Valley, Milcrofton and HB&TS utility districts. Electricity comes from Middle Tennessee Electric through TVA power, and gas from Atmos Energy. Find out which provider serves your address before a buyer asks.

sections.h2: Where a Franklin deed is recorded
sections.html:
Deeds for Franklin houses are filed with the Williamson County Register of Deeds at 1320 West Main Street, Suite 201, Franklin. Weekday hours are 8 to 4:30. The office posts a fee calculator, offers electronic filing and answers at 615-790-5706.

Recording also triggers state tax. The realty transfer tax is 37 cents for every $100 of the sale price, and the mortgage tax is 11.5 cents per $100 of a buyer's loan above the first $2,000. The register collects both and sends them on to the state.

Whether you sell through an agent, on your own or for cash, the closing steps look alike. A title company confirms who owns the house, finds the payoff on any loan, checks for unpaid taxes and prepares the deed. The buyer pays the transfer tax as grantee, and the contract settles anything else.

  • Gather your latest tax statement and the name of your lender before you accept an offer.
  • Ask the title company to confirm the payoff, the unpaid taxes and the recording steps before closing day.
  • Plan on the trustee statement being split between you and the buyer at the table, since the trustee will not prorate it.
  • Sign the deed, then let the title company carry it to the Register of Deeds.

A cash buyer skips lender approval and the appraisal, which removes two common sources of delay. You still need clean title, so the tax and payoff checks above apply to every route. If the house needs repairs, a cash offer simply prices them in and you avoid showings and repair requests after inspection.

faqs.q: How many people live in Franklin?
faqs.a: About 90,226 as of July 2025, up from 83,454 in 2020. Only six Tennessee cities have more people.

faqs.q: What is Franklin's city property tax rate?
faqs.a: It is $0.296 per $100 of assessed value, and the 2026-27 budget proposal keeps it there. County and school district charges appear on the same bill.

faqs.q: When are Williamson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They can be paid from the first Monday of October until the end of February. After that, interest of 1.5 percent is added and repeats monthly.

faqs.q: Who pays Tennessee's transfer tax on a Franklin sale?
faqs.a: The buyer does, as the grantee on the deed. The state rate is 37 cents per $100 of price, collected by the register at filing.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed for a Franklin house?
faqs.a: The Williamson County Register of Deeds, in Suite 201 at 1320 West Main Street. Staff there can answer fee questions at 615-790-5706.
